title: Existence of normalized finite Tate balancing and source compatibilities
statement: Let φ : A → B be a unital map of finite commutative rings killed by a positive integer N, and let X be a scheme on which N is invertible. For the actual scalar/single, shift, tensor and pullback comparisons and predicates in [def-pur-finite-tate-scalar-source-data], there exists a family β_r : Q_X(A_X(r)) ≅ B_X(r) satisfying the generator, degree-zero and tensor-power balancing equations, the single/unit and shifted-line normalization, invertibility of every unbounded source map, and the coefficient-unit and zero-power source equations. This assertion does not include uniqueness of β or the flat-single comparison for arbitrary flat sheaves.

source.place: paragraph 2, finite reduction: ordinary Tate balancing, scalar/single unit, tensor and shift source; old Step 7

proof.text: Apply the ordinary sectionwise coefficient construction to obtain a family β with the generator, degree-zero and successor balancing equations.
For this balancing family, the flat Tate-line calculation gives the specified single/unit and shifted-line normalization.
The tensorator, scalar/pullback comparison, and unit coherence give source invertibility and the coefficient-unit and zero-power source equations.

from.place: construction of the balancing family and its compatibilities

lean.statement:
theorem finite_tate_scalar_source_normalization_exists [Finite A] [Finite B]
    (φ : A →+* B) (N : ℕ) (hN : 0 < N)
    (hA : (N : A) = 0) (hB : (N : B) = 0)
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (hX : ∀ x : X, IsUnit (N : X.presheaf.stalk x)) :
    ∃ β : ∀ r : ℕ,
        (Etale.purityScalarSheaf φ X).obj (Scheme.finiteEtaleTateTwist X N A hA r) ≅
          Scheme.finiteEtaleTateTwist X N B hB r,
      IsFiniteTateScalarBalancing φ N hA hB X β ∧
      IsFiniteTateScalarLineNormalized φ N hA hB X β ∧
      IsFiniteTateScalarSourceInvertible φ N hA hB X β ∧
      IsFiniteTateScalarSourceUnitNormalized φ N hA hB X β ∧
      IsFiniteTateScalarSourceZeroNormalized φ N hA hB X β
